notes:
LOCATION: The list starts on n16.jpg (p. 1, the first page of the Eighth Report, stations 4–14) and continues on n17.jpg (p. 2, stations 15–29). n18.jpg (p. 3) has only the 'Diary from the Stations'. The section heading is 'EAST COAST OF SCOTLAND.' and the table itself is headed 'EAST OF SCOTLAND.'

COLUMNS: (1) 'Returns in 8 years, including 1886.', a count, or '1st' for a first return; (2) '1886. Actual returns.', where '*' marks a station that returned schedules in 1886; (3) map number and station, with a county or locality on the mainland rows; (4) 'Values.', the migration value I–V; (5) 'Feet.', the light's height. Sub-headings are printed in small capitals: 'Shetland.', 'Orkney.', 'Mainland.'. Feet are given only for Shetland 4–6 and for the mainland rows. Sumburgh Head and every Orkney row have no height. In 'other' I have labelled each value with its column.

NO KEEPERS OR CHARACTERS IN THE LIST: A note printed sideways in the right margin of both pages reads 'The names of the Reporters are given under "Diary from the Stations."' That is why every keepers field is []. The diary starts on p. 2: 'N. Unst.—John Nichol (principal) sends in seven well-filled schedules.' Later it calls him 'Mr Nichol' and 'Mr J. N.'. To get keepers' names for 1886 you will have to read the diary (p. 2 onward), not this table. The list gives no light characters.

PRINTING DETAILS: The 'B' in 26B and 28B is set in small capitals ('26B.Carr', '28B.Fidra', with no space after the full stop). Carr Rock and Fidra each take two printed lines, joined by a right brace '}', and both have '?' in the Values and Feet columns. In the Carr Rock row the line break falls in 'Fife / Coast'. In the Fidra row it falls in 'in- / stituted 1886'; I joined the word as 'instituted'. I took 'Lightship' as Carr Rock's type; it is printed as part of the name, 'Carr Rock Lightship'. St Abb's Head is set tightly as 'StAbb's Head,Berwickshire,', with no full stop after 'St'. In the name field I wrote it 'St Abb's Head'. I did not count the leader dots exactly, so their number in 'printed' is approximate.

UNCERTAIN MARK: In the Pentland Skerries row the 'actual returns' mark is a faint dash rather than a clear asterisk, so I wrote it as [?]. It is probably a poorly inked asterisk. The introduction says 'Pentland Skerries gives the heaviest returns with nine schedules' and 'Twelve stations ... have returned thirty-six schedules'. There are eleven clear asterisks, so Pentland Skerries would make twelve. Two faint specks near '13. Cantick Head' look like stray ink.

THINGS A READER SHOULD KNOW (copied as printed, not corrected):
- Dunnet Head's count in the 'Returns in 8 years' column is 18, which cannot be a number of years. Bell Rock's and Isle of May's 8 are possible. It may be a misprint, or the column may not count consistently.
- Chanonry Point is given as 'Elgin'. It is actually on the Black Isle, Ross-shire. This is noted as a slip, not corrected.
- Bell Rock (26) and Carr Rock (26B) are both placed on the 'Fife Coast'.
- 'Whalsey' is the old spelling of Whalsay. 'Girdleness' and 'Montroseness' are each printed as one word, but 'Buchan Ness' and 'Tarbat Ness' as two. 'Cromarty, East Cromarty' and 'Tarbat Ness, East Ross' are as printed.
- The introduction says schedules were sent to all stations except 'Tay Lightship and Carr Rock'. Tay Lightship does not appear in the list.
- The introduction says 'Then Bell Rock with two, and Fidra with three'. These are counts of schedules received in 1886, not the figures in the 8-year column. Fidra (28B) was 'instituted 1886', yet its 8-year count is 2.
- The OCR misreads several values (for example 'Wi.', 'We', 'Va', 'ie', 'LV') and some numbers ('98p' for 28B). The image readings above take precedence.
